title: Deductive Change Orders on Reconstruction Contracts: Signature and Credit
content:
A deductive change order removes scope from a Reconstruction contract, and its signed credit lowers the contract balance.

## Scope

For a deductive change order that a customer signs on a contract carrying exactly one change order proposal awaiting signature, and only for such a change order, the credit is worked out under the deductive change order credit rules. An additive change order is priced at its signature under the additive change order signature rule, never under these rules. Every deductive change order on a contract with more than one proposal awaiting signature is credited without markup at the base change order pricing of its line, install, finish and labor lines at the tier's rate times the quantity and flooring, cabinet and fixture upgrade lines at the owner's selected unit price less the tier's selection allowance, times the quantity, as the base change order rule states.

| Proposals awaiting signature on the contract | Credit worked out under |
|---|---|
| Exactly one (the deductive proposal) | the deductive change order credit rules |
| More than one | the base change order pricing of its line, without markup |

## The signature and what it records

The signature is the customer's own act: the customer signs the deductive proposal awaiting signature, and the signature records the credit worked out under these rules, on the records as they stand on the signing date, as the signed change order's amount and books it as one change order credit line naming that change order. The figure written on the proposal when it was drafted is not the credit. A deductive change order whose credit worked out under these rules is nothing is not written, because a change order and its credit line carry a positive amount.

## Invocation: `sign_deductive_change_order_5bfd6b95`

`sign_deductive_change_order_5bfd6b95` is a customer-owned tool: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it. One call marks the deductive proposal as signed and records the credit amount on it, adds one change order credit line dated today naming that change order and carrying the credit, and lowers the contract balance by the same amount. Afterwards the change order shows as signed with its credit amount, the credit line appears among the contract's payments and credits, and the contract balance is lower by the credit.

### Parameters

- `rebuild_contract_id` — the reference number of the customer's Reconstruction contract the deductive change order amends, as returned by the contract lookup.
- `change_order_id` — the reference number of the deductive change order proposal being signed, as returned by the change order lookup for that contract.
- `amount` — the credit amount the customer signs for, in US dollars, a number with exactly 2 decimal places; any further digits are rounded to the cent, half up.

### Return

A one-line confirmation naming the credit line reference (a text id beginning "rbp_"), the change order reference, the credit amount in US dollars with 2 decimals and the new contract balance in US dollars with 2 decimals. The presence of the credit line reference means the signature was recorded and the credit posted.
